messages:
erin: Heads-up — canary for new raven-lite-int4 shows ~2.7% parse failures but manual traces indicate the model is prepending short human text before the JSON payload (e.g. 'Here you go:' or 'Result ->').

cole: Got an example?

erin: Yep pasted one from request id 34f2a: 
```\nHere you go: {\n  \"items\": [{\"id\": 1, \"label\": \"foo\"}]\n}\n```\n
vikram: Ugh. That prefix breaks our strict parser. Is this only on streaming or also non-streamed responses?

erin: Mostly streaming int4 canaries but we saw a few non-streamed too. Pattern: short ascii prefix, often ends with ':' or '->' then valid JSON. No extra text after JSON.

maria: Two quick thoughts: 1) prompt engineering to force JSON-only usually helps but not perfect w/ quantized small models. 2) We should avoid blind string-trimming that could hide real model regressions.

sam: Agreed. Suggestion: implement a "soft-strip" heuristic in the parser which does: find first char that could start an object/array ("{" or "["), attempt to parse from there; if parse succeeds and schema validation passes, flag as rescue_applied and report. If not, fall back to existing retries.

cole: That seems reasonable. Want to capture failure modes in telemetry: prefix_length, first_start_char_index, repaired=true/false, schema_error_code.

vikram: Also add a streaming-aware variant: sometimes brace appears in token boundary chunks — we should attempt to accumulate up to N tokens after first brace to find matching closing brace rather than failing eagerly.

jules: What about malicious prefixes or cases where the prefix is actually important (e.g., the assistant includes an explanation)? We need to make sure rescue doesn't silently drop semantics.

maria: Schema validation will catch dropped fields. For human text that intentionally wraps JSON ("Explanation: {..}"), rescue is still okay as long as the JSON validates and tests pass. We should log the original response in S3 for audit when rescue_applied=true.

erin: Operational plan I propose:
- Short-term (canary): add soft-strip parser + streaming brace matcher + telemetry flags. Canary at 2% traffic for raven-lite-int4.
- Metrics to watch: parse_success_rate, post_rescue_validation_rate, latency p50/p95, rescue_fraction, downstream_error_rate.
- If rescue_fraction > 1% or post_rescue_validation_rate < 99.5% then roll back.

sam: Add experiment arm comparing: enforced system prompt ("OUTPUT ONLY JSON") vs soft-strip vs both. That will tell us whether prompt constraint or post-hoc repair is better for int4 quantized models.

vikram: One more gotcha: quantization can change tokenization slightly, leading to extra whitespace/newline tokens before the first brace. Make sure soft-strip ignores whitespace and common prefix tokens like "Assistant:" and emoji.

erin: I'll open a canary PR with parser change + telemetry + P0 autobackout if parse failure spike.

cole: Can we also run a synthetic fuzz test: take dev prompt set, generate 1000 samples from current int4 and fp16 models and measure prefix rates and parse rescue effectiveness?

jules: I'll own the fuzz harness. Will run today and post results in this thread.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy queued for raven-lite-int4 soft-strip parser at 02:00 UTC. Link: https://deploys/reddo/1786012345-canary-soft-strip

erin: Thanks — tagging @maria for policy/audit checklist for storing raw outputs.

maria: ack. Ensure KMS encryption for raw buckets and 90d retention unless security asks for longer.

cole: Nice. After fuzz run, we'll decide whether to bake the change or keep as middleware-only rescue.

jules: Fuzz run complete — quick summary: int4 prefix_rate=3.1%, fp16 prefix_rate=0.4%. Soft-strip repaired 94% of int4 failures and all repaired validated against schema. Posting full numbers in #ml-results shortly.

erin: Excellent. Let's proceed with canary and reconvene after 24h.

cole: FYI, if we see new classes of prefix (multiline explanation before JSON) we'll need an adaptive trimper rather than single-brace seek. Keep eyes on rescue_fraction trends. :eyes:
